words.ex: CSS in the head is render-blocking, so the browser waits for it before painting.
words.exT: CSS в head блокирует отрисовку: браузер ждёт его, прежде чем рисовать.

words.ex: The browser parses HTML into the DOM and CSS into the CSSOM.
words.exT: Браузер разбирает HTML в DOM, а CSS — в CSSOM.

words.ex: Scripts without async or defer slow down the critical rendering path.
words.exT: Скрипты без async или defer замедляют критический путь отрисовки.

words.ex: Changing width causes a reflow; changing colour causes only a repaint.
words.exT: Смена ширины вызывает перерасчёт раскладки, смена цвета — только перерисовку.

words.ex: Reading offsetHeight inside a loop of style changes causes layout thrashing.
words.exT: Чтение offsetHeight в цикле с изменением стилей вызывает пробуксовку раскладки.

words.ex: Transform and opacity animations can run on the compositor.
words.exT: Анимации transform и opacity могут выполняться в компоновщике.

words.ex: Screen readers rely on semantic HTML to navigate the page.
words.exT: Скринридеры опираются на семантический HTML, чтобы перемещаться по странице.

words.ex: A modal should trap focus and return it to the button when it closes.
words.exT: Модалка должна удерживать фокус и возвращать его на кнопку после закрытия.

words.ex: A div with onClick breaks keyboard navigation; a real button doesn't.
words.exT: div с onClick ломает навигацию с клавиатуры, настоящая кнопка — нет.

words.ex: Low colour contrast makes text hard to read for many users.
words.exT: Низкий контраст цвета мешает многим пользователям читать текст.

words.ex: In the box model, every element is content, padding, border and margin.
words.exT: В блочной модели каждый элемент — это содержимое, padding, border и margin.

words.ex: An absolute element is positioned against its containing block.
words.exT: Абсолютный элемент позиционируется относительно содержащего блока.

words.ex: z-index only works inside one stacking context.
words.exT: z-index работает только внутри одного контекста наложения.

a: to take out of the flow
words.ex: position: absolute takes the element out of the flow.
words.exT: position: absolute выводит элемент из потока.

words.ex: I write mobile-first CSS and add min-width media queries.
words.exT: Я пишу CSS сначала под мобильные и добавляю медиазапросы min-width.

words.ex: At the tablet breakpoint the sidebar moves under the content.
words.exT: На брейкпоинте планшета боковая панель уходит под контент.

words.ex: With a container query, a card adapts to its container, not the viewport.
words.exT: С контейнерным запросом карточка подстраивается под контейнер, а не под экран.

words.ex: Tailwind gives you utility classes instead of writing custom CSS.
words.exT: Tailwind даёт утилитарные классы вместо собственного CSS.

words.t: дизайн-токен (общее значение цвета, отступа и т.п.)
words.ex: Colours and spacing come from design tokens, so the UI stays consistent.
words.exT: Цвета и отступы берутся из дизайн-токенов, поэтому интерфейс единообразен.

words.ex: CSS Modules scope styles to one component automatically.
words.exT: CSS Modules автоматически ограничивают стили одним компонентом.

words.ex: JavaScript has seven primitives; everything else is an object.
words.exT: В JavaScript семь примитивов, всё остальное — объекты.

words.ex: Spread makes a shallow copy; structuredClone makes a deep copy.
words.exT: Spread делает поверхностную копию, structuredClone — глубокую.

words.ex: Because of event bubbling, a click on a list item reaches the list too.
words.exT: Из-за всплытия клик по пункту списка доходит и до самого списка.

words.ex: With event delegation, one listener on the parent handles all the items.
words.exT: При делегировании один обработчик на родителе обслуживает все пункты.

words.t: откладывать до паузы / ограничивать частоту вызовов
words.ex: I debounce the search input and throttle the scroll handler.
words.exT: Я откладываю поиск до паузы в вводе и ограничиваю частоту обработчика скролла.

words.ex: Named imports help tree shaking remove the code we don't use.
words.exT: Именованные импорты помогают при сборке удалить код, который мы не используем.

words.ex: A dynamic import loads the chart library only when the user opens the report.
words.exT: Динамический импорт загружает библиотеку графиков, только когда пользователь открывает отчёт.

words.ex: If you mutate state, the reference stays the same and React won't update.
words.exT: Если изменить состояние на месте, ссылка не поменяется и React не обновится.

words.ex: Fetching data is a side effect, so it goes into useEffect, not into render.
words.exT: Загрузка данных — побочный эффект, поэтому она в useEffect, а не в рендере.

words.ex: A reducer must be a pure function: same input, same output, no side effects.
words.exT: Редьюсер должен быть чистой функцией: тот же вход — тот же выход, без побочных эффектов.

words.ex: satisfies checks a value without type widening.
words.exT: satisfies проверяет значение без расширения типа.

words.ex: A type assertion only silences the compiler; it doesn't check anything at runtime.
words.exT: Утверждение типа лишь заглушает компилятор и ничего не проверяет во время выполнения.

words.ex: Partial and Omit are utility types built on mapped types.
words.exT: Partial и Omit — утилитарные типы на основе mapped types.

words.ex: Interfaces support declaration merging, so we can extend library types.
words.exT: Интерфейсы поддерживают слияние объявлений, поэтому можно дополнять типы библиотек.

words.ex: We commit the lock file so every machine installs the same versions.
words.exT: Мы коммитим лок-файл, чтобы на всех машинах ставились одни и те же версии.

words.ex: Under semantic versioning, a major version means breaking changes.
words.exT: При семантическом версионировании мажорная версия означает несовместимые изменения.

words.ex: React is a peer dependency of a component library.
words.exT: React — peer-зависимость библиотеки компонентов.

words.ex: The bundler transpiles, minifies and splits the code into chunks.
words.exT: Сборщик транспилирует, минифицирует и делит код на чанки.

words.ex: Vite transpiles TypeScript and JSX on the fly in development.
words.exT: В разработке Vite транспилирует TypeScript и JSX на лету.

words.ex: A content hash in the file name lets us cache files for a year.
words.exT: Хеш содержимого в имени файла позволяет кешировать файлы на год.

words.ex: Hot module replacement updates the page without losing state.
words.exT: Горячая замена модулей обновляет страницу без потери состояния.

words.ex: I cherry-picked the hotfix commit into the release branch.
words.exT: Я перенёс коммит с хотфиксом в релизную ветку.

words.ex: Cleanup runs before the next effect and when the component unmounts.
words.exT: Очистка выполняется перед следующим эффектом и при размонтировании компонента.

words.ex: Changing the key makes React remount the component and reset its state.
words.exT: Смена key заставляет React перемонтировать компонент и сбросить его состояние.

words.ex: I use stable keys from the data, not the array index.
words.exT: Я использую стабильные ключи из данных, а не индекс массива.

words.ex: React Hook Form uses uncontrolled inputs to avoid re-renders.
words.exT: React Hook Form использует неуправляемые поля, чтобы избежать ререндеров.

words.ex: Context helps avoid prop drilling through five levels of components.
words.exT: Context помогает не пробрасывать пропсы через пять уровней компонентов.

words.ex: I extracted the fetching logic into a custom hook.
words.exT: Я вынес логику загрузки данных в кастомный хук.

words.ex: An error boundary shows a fallback instead of a white screen.
words.exT: Граница ошибок показывает запасной UI вместо белого экрана.

words.ex: I render the modal through a portal at the end of the body.
words.exT: Я рендерю модалку через портал в конец body.

words.ex: Concurrent rendering lets React pause work and handle urgent updates first.
words.exT: Конкурентный рендеринг позволяет React приостановить работу и сначала обработать срочные обновления.

words.ex: With an optimistic update, the like appears before the server answers.
words.exT: При оптимистичном обновлении лайк появляется до ответа сервера.

words.ex: Server Components send no JavaScript; Client Components handle interactivity.
words.exT: Серверные компоненты не отправляют JavaScript, клиентские отвечают за интерактивность.

words.ex: Don't copy server data into a global store; keep it in the query cache.
words.exT: Не копируйте серверные данные в глобальное хранилище — держите их в кеше запросов.

words.ex: With a selector, the component re-renders only when its slice changes.
words.exT: С селектором компонент перерисовывается, только когда меняется его часть состояния.

words.ex: Redux Toolkit removes most of the old Redux boilerplate.
words.exT: Redux Toolkit убирает большую часть старого шаблонного кода Redux.

words.ex: Stale-while-revalidate shows cached data instantly and refreshes it in the background.
words.exT: Stale-while-revalidate сразу показывает данные из кеша и обновляет их в фоне.

words.ex: The search term is part of the query key, so old responses can't win.
words.exT: Поисковый запрос входит в ключ запроса, поэтому старые ответы не победят.

words.ex: Server-side rendering gives a fast first paint and good SEO.
words.exT: Рендеринг на сервере даёт быструю первую отрисовку и хорошее SEO.

words.ex: Static site generation builds the blog pages once at build time.
words.exT: Статическая генерация собирает страницы блога один раз при сборке.

words.ex: With incremental static regeneration, product pages refresh in the background.
words.exT: При инкрементальной регенерации страницы товаров обновляются в фоне.

words.ex: Using Date.now() in render can cause a hydration mismatch.
words.exT: Date.now() в рендере может вызвать несовпадение при гидратации.

words.ex: Streaming sends each part of the page as soon as it's ready.
words.exT: Потоковая отдача отправляет каждую часть страницы, как только она готова.

words.t: на первом экране / ниже первого экрана
words.ex: Images below the fold are lazy-loaded.
words.exT: Картинки ниже первого экрана загружаются лениво.

words.ex: A bundle analyser shows what makes the bundle size so big.
words.exT: Анализатор бандла показывает, что раздувает его размер.

words.ex: We added a performance budget to CI so the bundle can't grow unnoticed.
words.exT: Мы добавили в CI бюджет производительности, чтобы бандл не рос незаметно.

words.ex: Heavy JavaScript on the main thread makes INP worse.
words.exT: Тяжёлый JavaScript в главном потоке ухудшает INP.

words.ex: Always sanitise HTML before passing it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
words.exT: Всегда очищайте HTML перед передачей в dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

words.ex: A Content Security Policy blocks scripts from unknown sources.
words.exT: Политика безопасности контента блокирует скрипты из неизвестных источников.

words.ex: XSS happens when untrusted input runs as code in the browser.
words.exT: XSS — это когда недоверенный ввод выполняется в браузере как код.

words.ex: SameSite cookies are not sent with most cross-site requests.
words.exT: Cookie с SameSite не отправляются с большинством межсайтовых запросов.

words.ex: Good tests check behaviour, not implementation details.
words.exT: Хорошие тесты проверяют поведение, а не детали реализации.

words.ex: MSW intercepts requests at the network level.
words.exT: MSW перехватывает запросы на уровне сети.

words.ex: Every test should end with a clear assertion.
words.exT: Каждый тест должен заканчиваться понятной проверкой.

words.ex: After deploy we run a smoke test of login and checkout.
words.exT: После деплоя мы прогоняем дымовой тест входа и оформления заказа.

words.ex: E2E tests cover only critical user flows like login and payment.
words.exT: E2E-тесты покрывают только ключевые сценарии: вход и оплату.

words.ex: In short, defer keeps the order and async doesn't.
words.exT: Короче говоря, defer сохраняет порядок, а async — нет.

words.ex: The reason is that React compares references.
words.exT: Причина в том, что React сравнивает ссылки.

words.ex: It depends on how often the data changes.
words.exT: Это зависит от того, как часто меняются данные.

words.ex: As a rule of thumb, I don't memoise until I see a problem in the Profiler.
words.exT: Как правило, я не мемоизирую, пока не увижу проблему в профайлере.

words.w: the first thing I'd do is measure it
words.t: первым делом я бы это измерил
a: first thing I'd do is measure it
words.ex: The first thing I'd do is measure it with the React Profiler.
words.exT: Первым делом я бы измерил это профайлером React.

words.w: I haven't used it in production, but …
words.t: я не использовал это в продакшене, но …
a: I haven't used it in production
words.ex: I haven't used it in production, but as I understand it, it caches server data.
words.exT: Я не использовал это в продакшене, но, насколько я понимаю, это кеш серверных данных.

words.ex: TanStack Query gives you retries and caching out of the box.
words.exT: TanStack Query даёт повторы и кеширование из коробки.

words.ex: A common pitfall is using the index as a key.
words.exT: Частая ошибка — использовать индекс в качестве ключа.

words.ex: Keep in mind that CORS doesn't protect the API from curl.
words.exT: Имейте в виду, что CORS не защищает API от curl.

words.ex: Let me think out loud while I write this.
words.exT: Позвольте порассуждать вслух, пока я пишу код.

words.ex: To put it simply, a closure is a function with a backpack of variables.
words.exT: Проще говоря, замыкание — это функция с рюкзаком переменных.

words.w: What happens when you open a URL?
words.t: The browser finds the server, downloads the page, and turns code into pixels: DNS → connection → HTML → DOM + CSSOM → layout → paint.
a: What happens when you open a URL
words.ex: First the browser resolves the domain with DNS and opens a secure connection. It gets HTML back, builds the DOM from HTML and the CSSOM from CSS, then calculates the layout, paints, and shows the result. Scripts without async or defer can block this process.
words.exT: DNS → соединение → HTML; из HTML строится DOM, из CSS — CSSOM, затем раскладка, отрисовка, показ.

words.w: async vs defer on a script tag?
words.t: Both download in the background; defer runs after parsing and keeps order, async runs as soon as it's loaded.
a: async vs defer on a script tag
words.ex: Both load scripts without blocking the HTML. Defer runs them after parsing, in order, so it's right for app code. Async runs each script the moment it arrives, so it suits independent things like analytics.
words.exT: Оба грузят без блокировки; defer — после разбора и по порядку, async — сразу по загрузке.

words.w: Why do semantic HTML and accessibility matter?
words.t: The right tag gives meaning to people, screen readers and search engines — and keyboard support for free.
a: Why do semantic HTML and accessibility matter
words.ex: Semantic HTML means using elements for their meaning, like button, nav or label. Screen readers rely on it, it helps SEO, and native elements give keyboard support for free. I also add alt text, labels, keyboard support and focus management in modals.
words.exT: Правильные теги дают смысл скринридерам и поиску и поддержку клавиатуры бесплатно.

words.t: Reflow recalculates positions and is expensive; repaint only redraws pixels. Animate transform and opacity.
words.ex: Reflow happens when geometry changes and the browser recalculates the layout. Repaint is cheaper: only pixels change. For smooth animations I use transform and opacity, because they can skip layout and paint.
words.exT: Reflow пересчитывает геометрию (дорого), repaint только перерисовывает. Анимировать transform и opacity.

words.w: localStorage vs sessionStorage vs cookies vs IndexedDB?
words.t: localStorage persists, sessionStorage lives per tab, cookies travel with requests, IndexedDB holds big data.
a: localStorage vs sessionStorage vs cookies vs IndexedDB
words.ex: LocalStorage keeps data until it's cleared, sessionStorage only for one tab. Both are readable by JavaScript, so XSS could steal a token from there. For auth I prefer HttpOnly cookies. For large offline data there's IndexedDB.
words.exT: localStorage — навсегда, sessionStorage — на вкладку, cookie уходят с запросами, IndexedDB — для больших данных.

words.t: Every element is content + padding + border + margin; border-box makes width include padding and border.
words.ex: Each element is a box: content, padding, border and margin. By default width applies only to the content, so padding makes the box bigger. With border-box, width includes padding and border, which is why most projects use it.
words.exT: Элемент = контент + padding + border + margin; border-box включает padding и border в ширину.

words.t: When rules conflict, the more specific selector wins: inline > ID > class > tag; on a tie, the later rule wins.
words.ex: Specificity decides which rule wins. IDs beat classes, classes beat tags, and inline styles beat all of them. If two rules are equal, the last one wins. I keep specificity low, mostly single classes, so styles are easy to override.
words.exT: Побеждает более специфичный селектор: inline > id > класс > тег; при равенстве — последний.

words.t: Flexbox is one-dimensional (a row or a column); Grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns together).
words.ex: Flexbox lays items out in a row or a column. Grid handles rows and columns at the same time. I use flex for components like toolbars and grid for page layouts, and often combine them.
words.exT: Flex — одно направление, Grid — строки и колонки сразу.

words.w: What are the CSS position values?
words.t: static is default; relative shifts but keeps space; absolute leaves the flow; fixed sticks to the screen; sticky sticks after scrolling.
a: What are the CSS position values
words.ex: Relative shifts the element but keeps its space. Absolute removes it from the flow and places it against the nearest positioned parent. Fixed is attached to the viewport, and sticky behaves normally until a scroll point, then sticks.
words.exT: relative — сдвиг с сохранением места, absolute — вне потока, fixed — к экрану, sticky — прилипает при скролле.

words.t: z-index only compares elements inside the same stacking context.
words.ex: Properties like transform or opacity create a new stacking context, so a child with a huge z-index still can't go above another context. That's why modals are usually rendered through a portal at the end of the body.
words.exT: z-index сравнивается только внутри одного контекста наложения.

words.w: How do you build a responsive layout?
words.t: Mobile-first CSS, min-width media queries, flexible units (rem, %, fr), flex and grid, responsive images.
a: How do you build a responsive layout
words.ex: I start mobile-first and add media queries for larger screens. I use flexible units, mostly rem, plus flex and grid, and responsive images with srcset. Rem is relative to the root font size, while em compounds when nested.
words.exT: Сначала мобильные, медиазапросы min-width, гибкие единицы, flex/grid, srcset.

words.w: BEM vs CSS Modules vs CSS-in-JS vs Tailwind?
words.t: They all solve the same problem — styles leaking into each other — in different ways.
a: BEM vs CSS Modules vs CSS-in-JS vs Tailwind
words.ex: The main problem in CSS is global scope. BEM solves it with naming, CSS Modules with build-time scoping, CSS-in-JS by keeping styles in components. Tailwind uses utility classes: fast and consistent, though the markup gets long.
words.exT: Все решают глобальность CSS: имена, области при сборке, стили в компонентах, утилиты.

words.w: What are the data types? == vs ===?
words.t: === compares value and type; == converts types first. 7 primitives + objects.
a: What are the data types? == vs ===
words.ex: JavaScript has seven primitive types, and everything else is an object. Double equals converts types before comparing, which gives surprising results, so I always use triple equals.
words.exT: === без приведения типов, == с приведением; 7 примитивов + объекты.

words.w: var vs let vs const and hoisting?
words.t: var is function-scoped and hoisted as undefined; let and const are block-scoped and in the TDZ until declared.
a: var vs let vs const and hoisting
words.ex: Var is function-scoped and hoisted with undefined. Let and const are block-scoped and throw an error if used before declaration. Const only prevents reassignment, so a const object can still be mutated.
words.exT: var — функция, undefined; let/const — блок, TDZ; const запрещает переприсваивание, не изменение.

words.t: A function remembers the variables from where it was created, even after that scope is gone.
words.ex: A closure is a function plus the variables from the scope where it was created. It keeps access to them after that scope is gone. I use closures for private state and things like debounce, and every React hook relies on them.
words.exT: Функция помнит переменные места, где создана.

words.t: By how the function is called, not where it's written; arrow functions take it from outside.
words.ex: Called on an object, this is that object. With new, it's the new instance. Call, apply and bind set it explicitly. Arrow functions don't have their own this, which is why they're handy in callbacks.
words.exT: this зависит от способа вызова; у стрелочных функций своего this нет.

words.w: How do prototypes and classes work?
words.t: A missing property is looked up the prototype chain; classes are nicer syntax over prototypes.
a: How do prototypes and classes work
words.ex: Every object links to a prototype. When a property is missing, JavaScript walks up the chain until it finds it or reaches null. Classes are mostly syntax sugar over this, with extras like private fields.
words.exT: Свойство ищется по цепочке прототипов; классы — синтаксис поверх прототипов.

words.t: Sync code first, then all microtasks (promises), then one macrotask (timer, event), maybe a render — repeat.
words.ex: JavaScript is single-threaded. First the synchronous code runs. Then the engine empties the microtask queue with promise callbacks. Then it takes one macrotask, like a timer or an event, and the browser can render. So a promise callback always runs before setTimeout with zero delay.
words.exT: Синхронный код → все микрозадачи → одна макрозадача → отрисовка → снова.

words.w: Promise.all vs allSettled vs race vs any?
words.t: all fails on the first error; allSettled waits for all; race takes the first to finish; any takes the first success.
a: Promise.all vs allSettled vs race vs any
words.ex: Promise.all fails fast if one promise fails. AllSettled waits for everything and never fails. Race settles with the first finished promise, so it's used for timeouts. Any takes the first successful one.
words.exT: all падает на первой ошибке, allSettled ждёт все, race — первый завершившийся, any — первый успешный.

words.t: Debounce waits until calls stop; throttle limits how often a call can happen.
words.ex: Debounce delays a call until events stop for some time, which is perfect for a search box. Throttle lets a call happen at most once per interval, which suits scroll handlers.
words.exT: Debounce ждёт паузы, throttle ограничивает частоту.

words.w: What are event bubbling and delegation?
words.t: Events travel up to the parents, so one parent listener can handle many children.
a: What are event bubbling and delegation
words.ex: When you click an element, the event bubbles up through its parents. With delegation, I put one listener on the parent and check event.target. That means fewer listeners, and it works for items added later.
words.exT: События всплывают к родителям, поэтому один обработчик на родителе обслуживает всех детей.

words.t: A shallow copy shares nested objects; a deep copy duplicates everything (structuredClone).
words.ex: Spread only copies the top level, so nested objects are still shared. For a deep copy I use structuredClone. In React this matters because change detection compares references: if I mutate, the UI won't update.
words.exT: Поверхностная копия делит вложенные объекты, глубокая копирует всё.

words.w: ES modules vs CommonJS, and what is tree shaking?
words.t: import/export are static, so bundlers can remove unused code — that's tree shaking.
a: ES modules vs CommonJS, and what is tree shaking
words.ex: ES modules are static, so a bundler can see what's actually used and remove the rest. Dynamic import loads code on demand, which is the basis of code splitting. CommonJS is dynamic and harder to optimise.
words.exT: Статические import/export позволяют сборщику выбросить неиспользуемый код.

words.t: Both describe shapes; interface can merge and extend, type can also describe unions and computed types.
words.ex: Interfaces can merge declarations, which helps when extending library types. Type aliases are more flexible: unions, tuples, mapped types. I use interfaces for object contracts and types for everything else.
words.exT: Оба описывают форму; interface сливается, type умеет объединения и вычисляемые типы.

words.t: any turns checking off, unknown forces you to check first, never means "impossible".
words.ex: Any disables type checking, so I avoid it. Unknown is the safe version: TypeScript makes me check the type before using the value. Never means a value that can't exist, and I use it to make sure a switch handles every case.
words.exT: any выключает проверку, unknown требует проверки, never — невозможное значение.

words.t: Type parameters, so one function works with many types without losing information.
words.ex: Generics are parameters for types. They let me write one function that works with any type and still keeps the exact type in the result. With extends I can limit which types are allowed.
words.exT: Параметры для типов: одна функция для многих типов без потери информации.

words.w: Which utility types do you use?
words.t: Ready-made tools to build new types: Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType.
a: Which utility types do you use
words.ex: Utility types transform existing types. For example, Partial for an update form where every field is optional, or Omit to remove the id from a create DTO. Under the hood they're mapped types.
words.exT: Готовые инструменты для создания типов из существующих.

words.w: What are narrowing and discriminated unions?
words.t: After a check, TypeScript knows the exact type; a shared field like status tells the variants apart.
a: What are narrowing and discriminated unions
words.ex: Narrowing means TypeScript knows a more specific type after a check. A discriminated union is a set of types with a common field, like status. When I switch on it, TypeScript knows exactly which fields exist in each branch.
words.exT: После проверки TS сужает тип; общее поле status различает варианты.

words.w: What do ^ and ~ mean, and why a lock file?
words.t: package.json says what you allow, the lock file says exactly what you installed.
a: What do ^ and ~ mean, and why a lock file
words.ex: Package.json defines version ranges: caret allows minor updates, tilde only patches. The lock file pins exact versions of the whole tree. I commit it and use npm ci in pipelines, so every build is reproducible.
words.exT: package.json задаёт диапазоны, лок-файл — точные версии.

words.w: What does a bundler do? Why is Vite fast?
words.t: A bundler turns many source files into a few optimised files; Vite serves native modules on demand in development.
a: What does a bundler do? Why is Vite fast
words.ex: A bundler compiles TypeScript and JSX, removes unused code, minifies and splits it into chunks. Vite is fast in development because it doesn't bundle everything up front — it serves modules as the browser asks for them.
words.exT: Сборщик делает из многих файлов несколько оптимизированных; Vite в разработке отдаёт модули по запросу.

words.t: Merge keeps history as it was; rebase rewrites it into a straight line. Never rebase shared branches.
words.ex: Merge combines branches and keeps the full history. Rebase moves my commits on top of the main branch, so history is linear, but it rewrites commits. I rebase my own feature branch, and never shared branches.
words.exT: merge сохраняет историю, rebase переписывает её в линию; общие ветки не ребейзить.

words.w: When does a React component re-render?
words.t: When its state changes, its parent re-renders, or a context it uses changes.
a: When does a React component re-render
words.ex: React first renders a new tree, compares it with the old one, and then commits only the real differences to the DOM. So a re-render doesn't always mean a DOM update.
words.exT: При смене состояния, ререндере родителя или смене контекста.

words.w: What are the virtual DOM, reconciliation and Fiber?
words.t: React compares a lightweight copy of the UI and updates only what changed; Fiber lets it pause and prioritise.
a: What are the virtual DOM, reconciliation and Fiber
words.ex: React keeps a virtual description of the UI. After an update it compares the new tree with the old one — reconciliation — and changes only the necessary DOM nodes. Fiber splits this work into small pieces, so React can handle urgent updates first.
words.exT: React сравнивает лёгкую копию UI и меняет только отличия; Fiber позволяет прерывать работу.

words.w: Why are keys important? Why not the index?
words.t: Keys tell React which list item is which; the index breaks when items are added, removed or sorted.
a: Why are keys important? Why not the index
words.ex: Keys help React match list items between renders. If I use the index and the list is reordered, React attaches state to the wrong items, for example an input keeps the wrong text. So I use stable ids.
words.exT: Ключи сопоставляют элементы списка; индекс ломается при перестановках.

words.w: What are the rules of hooks?
words.t: Call hooks at the top level, in the same order every render — React tracks them by order.
a: What are the rules of hooks
words.ex: Hooks must be called at the top level, never inside conditions or loops. React doesn't know hooks by name — it remembers them by order. If the order changes, state goes to the wrong hook.
words.exT: Хуки только на верхнем уровне: React различает их по порядку вызова.

words.t: It syncs the component with something outside React; dependencies decide when it re-runs; cleanup undoes it.
words.ex: UseEffect is for side effects like subscriptions, timers or API calls. It runs after render, and the dependency array controls when it runs again. The cleanup removes listeners or timers. A common mistake is using an effect for data that could be calculated in render.
words.exT: Синхронизация с внешним миром; зависимости — когда перезапускать; очистка — отменить.

words.w: What is a stale closure in React?
words.t: A callback keeps an old value because it was created in an old render.
a: What is a stale closure in React
words.ex: Each render creates new functions that see the values of that render. If an interval is created once, it keeps seeing the first value forever. I fix it with a functional state update, correct dependencies, or a ref.
words.exT: Колбэк видит старое значение, потому что создан в старом рендере.

words.t: Tools to skip unnecessary work — memo skips a child render, useCallback keeps a function, useMemo keeps a value.
words.ex: React.memo skips a re-render when props are the same. UseCallback and useMemo keep references stable, so memo actually works. I don't add them everywhere, because they have a cost — I use them after profiling or for expensive calculations.
words.exT: Инструменты, чтобы не делать лишнюю работу; применять после замеров.

words.t: A box for a value that survives renders and doesn't cause re-renders.
words.ex: UseRef holds a mutable value that persists between renders, and changing it doesn't re-render the component. I use it for DOM access and for values like timer ids. If the UI depends on a value, it should be state.
words.exT: Изменяемое значение между рендерами без ререндера.

words.t: useLayoutEffect runs before the screen is painted, useEffect after.
words.ex: Both run after the DOM updates, but useLayoutEffect runs before the browser paints. I use it only when I need to measure something, like a tooltip position, to avoid a visible jump.
words.exT: useLayoutEffect — до отрисовки экрана, useEffect — после.

words.t: When state logic is complex or several values change together.
words.ex: I switch to useReducer when state logic gets complex or several fields change together. All transitions live in one pure reducer function, which is easier to read and test, and dispatch is stable.
words.exT: Для сложной логики состояния и связанных полей.

words.t: Controlled — React holds the value; uncontrolled — the DOM holds it.
words.ex: In a controlled input, React state is the source of truth, which makes validation easy but re-renders on every keystroke. In an uncontrolled input the DOM keeps the value. For big forms I use React Hook Form, which is built on uncontrolled inputs.
words.exT: Управляемое — значение в React, неуправляемое — в DOM.

words.w: What's the performance problem with Context?
words.t: When a context value changes, every component using it re-renders.
a: What's the performance problem with Context
words.ex: Context is great for rarely changing data like theme or the current user. But all consumers re-render when the value changes. So I memoise the value, split big contexts, and use Zustand or Redux for state that changes often.
words.exT: При смене значения контекста ререндерятся все потребители.

words.t: A function starting with "use" that reuses hook logic between components.
words.ex: A custom hook extracts reusable logic, for example data fetching. Each component that uses it gets its own state. In a useFetch hook I add an AbortController, so an old request can't overwrite newer data.
words.exT: Функция use… для переиспользования логики хуков; состояние у каждого своё.

words.t: A component that catches render errors in its children and shows a fallback.
words.ex: An error boundary catches errors during rendering and shows a fallback instead of a white screen. It doesn't catch errors in event handlers or promises — I handle those with try/catch.
words.exT: Ловит ошибки рендера детей и показывает запасной UI.

words.w: What are Suspense, lazy and portals for?
words.t: lazy loads code on demand, Suspense shows a fallback while waiting, a portal renders elsewhere in the DOM.
a: What are Suspense, lazy and portals for
words.ex: React.lazy loads a component only when it's needed, and Suspense shows a loader meanwhile. I use them to split the app by routes. Portals render into another DOM node, which helps modals escape overflow or z-index problems.
words.exT: lazy — код по требованию, Suspense — заглушка, портал — рендер в другой узел.

words.t: 18 made rendering interruptible; 19 made forms and async work simpler.
words.ex: React 18 brought concurrent rendering and automatic batching. With useTransition I can mark an update as non-urgent, so typing stays smooth. React 19 added Actions and hooks like useOptimistic, and made Server Components stable.
words.exT: 18 — прерываемый рендеринг, 19 — проще формы и асинхронность.

words.t: Components that run only on the server and send no JavaScript to the browser.
words.ex: Server Components run on the server, fetch data close to the source, and send no JavaScript for themselves. Interactive parts are Client Components marked with 'use client'. The result is a smaller bundle and faster loading.
words.exT: Компоненты только на сервере, без JavaScript в браузере.

words.t: Choose by type: server data → TanStack Query, local UI → useState, shared → Zustand/Redux, filters → URL.
words.ex: First I ask what kind of state it is. Data from the API goes to TanStack Query. Local UI state stays in the component. Shared client state goes to Zustand or Redux. Filters live in the URL so links are shareable. The common mistake is copying server data into a global store.
words.exT: Выбор по типу: серверные данные, локальное, общее, URL.

words.w: What is Redux and what does Redux Toolkit improve?
words.t: One store, changed only by actions through pure reducers; Toolkit removes boilerplate.
a: What is Redux and what does Redux Toolkit improve
words.ex: Redux keeps app state in one store. Components dispatch actions, and reducers return new state. Redux Toolkit is the modern way: createSlice reduces boilerplate, and Immer lets me write simple mutating code that stays immutable.
words.exT: Одно хранилище, изменения через actions и чистые редьюсеры; Toolkit убирает шаблонный код.

words.w: TanStack Query vs Zustand vs Redux Toolkit?
words.t: TanStack Query is for server data; Zustand and Redux are for client state.
a: TanStack Query vs Zustand vs Redux Toolkit
words.ex: TanStack Query isn't a global store — it's a cache for server data, and it replaces a lot of what Redux used to do. For client state I pick Zustand for small and medium apps and Redux Toolkit for large apps with complex logic.
words.exT: TanStack Query — кеш серверных данных; Zustand и Redux — клиентское состояние.

words.t: Show cached data immediately, refresh it in the background.
words.ex: The user sees cached data instantly, while a fresh request runs in the background and updates the screen. After a mutation I invalidate the related queries so lists stay up to date.
words.exT: Сразу показать данные из кеша и обновить их в фоне.

words.w: CSR vs SSR vs SSG vs ISR?
words.t: The difference is when and where the HTML is created: browser, every request, build time, or build time plus refresh.
a: CSR vs SSR vs SSG vs ISR
words.ex: CSR renders in the browser — simple, but slower first load and weaker SEO. SSR renders on each request, good for personalised pages. SSG builds pages once and is very fast. ISR is static pages that regenerate in the background.
words.exT: Разница — где и когда создаётся HTML.

words.t: React makes server HTML interactive by attaching event handlers; the first client render must match.
words.ex: The server sends HTML, and React hydrates it by connecting the event handlers. If the first client render differs from the server HTML, for example because of dates or window, we get a hydration mismatch. I move browser-only logic into an effect.
words.exT: React «оживляет» серверный HTML; первый рендер на клиенте должен совпасть.

words.w: What are the key ideas of the App Router?
words.t: Folders are routes, and components are Server Components by default.
a: What are the key ideas of the App Router
words.ex: In the App Router, the folder structure defines routes. Layouts wrap pages, and loading and error files add Suspense and error boundaries automatically. Components are server-side by default, and I add 'use client' only where I need interactivity.
words.exT: Папки — маршруты, компоненты по умолчанию серверные.

words.t: Three user-experience numbers: LCP ≤ 2.5 s (loading), INP ≤ 200 ms (reaction), CLS ≤ 0.1 (layout jumps).
words.ex: LCP measures when the main content appears — I improve it with optimised images and server rendering. INP measures how fast the page reacts — I reduce heavy JavaScript on the main thread. CLS measures layout jumps — I set image sizes and reserve space.
words.exT: Три метрики: скорость загрузки, отклика и стабильность вёрстки.

words.w: How do you make an app load faster?
words.t: Measure first, then ship less and ship it smarter.
a: How do you make an app load faster
words.ex: I always measure first. Then I split code by routes, remove or replace heavy libraries, and optimise images. Static files get hashed names and long caching, and are served through a CDN.
words.exT: Сначала замер, потом меньше кода и умнее доставка.

words.w: How do you render a list of 10,000 items?
words.t: Render only what the user can see — virtualisation.
a: How do you render a list of 10,000 items
words.ex: For ten thousand rows I use virtualisation: only visible rows are in the DOM, and they're reused while scrolling. Another option is server-side pagination. Stable keys and memoised rows help too.
words.exT: Рендерить только видимые строки — виртуализация.

words.w: What is XSS and how do you prevent it in React?
words.t: An attacker's script runs on your page; React escapes text, so watch dangerouslySetInnerHTML and links.
a: What is XSS and how do you prevent it in React
words.ex: XSS is when untrusted input runs as code in the user's browser. React escapes values by default, so the risk comes from dangerouslySetInnerHTML or unsafe links. I sanitise HTML, add a Content Security Policy, and keep tokens in HttpOnly cookies.
words.exT: Чужой скрипт выполняется на странице; React экранирует текст, опасны innerHTML и ссылки.

words.t: Another site makes the user's browser send a request with their cookies.
words.ex: CSRF uses the fact that cookies are sent automatically. A malicious site can trigger a request as the logged-in user. SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens prevent it, and GET requests should never change data.
words.exT: Чужой сайт отправляет запрос от имени пользователя с его cookie.

words.w: What is the idea of React Testing Library?
words.t: Test what the user sees and does, not the code inside.
a: What is the idea of React Testing Library
words.ex: RTL tests behaviour from the user's point of view. I find elements by role or label, click and type like a user, and check what's on the screen. I don't test internal state, so tests survive refactoring.
words.exT: Тестировать то, что видит и делает пользователь, а не внутренности.

words.t: get — must exist, query — may not exist, find — will appear later.
words.ex: I use getBy for elements that must be there, queryBy to assert that something isn't there, and findBy for content that appears after loading. For the API I use MSW, which intercepts network requests.
words.exT: get — обязан быть, query — может отсутствовать, find — появится позже.

words.w: What does the frontend testing pyramid look like?
words.t: Many fast tests at the bottom, a few slow ones at the top: unit → component (RTL) → E2E.
a: What does the frontend testing pyramid look like
words.ex: I write many unit tests, a good layer of component tests with RTL, and a few end-to-end tests with Playwright for critical flows. TypeScript and ESLint catch many bugs before tests even run.
words.exT: Много быстрых тестов внизу, немного медленных наверху.

words.w: A form re-renders the whole page on every keystroke. What do you do?
words.t: Measure with the Profiler, move state down, use uncontrolled inputs (React Hook Form), memoise heavy siblings.
a: form re-renders the whole page on every keystroke. What do you do?
A form re-renders the whole page on every keystroke. What do you do
form re-renders the whole page on every keystroke. What do you do
words.ex: First I confirm it with the React Profiler. Usually the form state lives too high, so I move it down into the form. For big forms I use React Hook Form with uncontrolled inputs. I memoise heavy sibling components and debounce expensive validation.
words.exT: Замерить, опустить состояние вниз, неуправляемые поля, мемоизировать тяжёлое.

words.w: Search sometimes shows results for an old query. Why?
words.t: A race condition: an older, slower response arrives last. Abort old requests or use the query key.
a: Search sometimes shows results for an old query. Why
words.ex: An older, slower response arrives after the newer one and overwrites it. I cancel the previous request with AbortController or ignore stale responses. TanStack Query solves it because the search term is part of the query key. I also debounce the input.
words.exT: Гонка запросов: старый медленный ответ приходит последним.

words.w: Users double-click "Pay" and get two orders. How do you fix it?
words.t: Disable the button while pending, but the real fix is an idempotency key on the backend.
a: Users double-click "Pay" and get two orders. How do you fix it
words.ex: On the frontend I disable the button and show a loader while the request is running. But the real protection is on the backend: an idempotency key, so a repeated request returns the same result instead of creating a second order.
words.exT: Блокировать кнопку, но главное — ключ идемпотентности на бэкенде.

words.w: The bundle is 3 MB. Where do you start?
words.t: Open a bundle analyser, then split by routes, lazy-load heavy widgets, replace heavy libraries, add a size budget.
a: bundle is 3 MB. Where do you start?
The bundle is 3 MB. Where do you start
bundle is 3 MB. Where do you start
words.ex: I open a bundle analyser to see what's inside. Usually it's a huge library imported for one function, or a heavy chart or editor loaded on every page. I split code by routes, lazy-load heavy widgets, replace heavy libraries, and add a size limit in CI.
words.exT: Анализатор бандла, разделение по маршрутам, ленивая загрузка, лимит размера.
